external:vault: Vault encrypted secrets, decrypted-secret view and credential references; shared service custody, never included as raw values or treated as empty subject copies.
external:net: pg_net pending HTTP requests and response custody, including dispatch headers and bodies; shared/provider work with possible unresolved effects, always blocked for personal erasure.
external:cron: pg_cron job and job_run_details metadata plus scheduler service logs; shared operational custody with no approved personal selector or erasure adapter.
external:supabase_migrations: Unlinked control-only installation/migration lineage, including collect_installation_steps profile/source/rendered SQL hashes, operation identity and timestamps. Immutable provenance must be included in full database recovery; no personal erasure adapter.

qualification: Database row hashes and actual protected-object probes do not establish erasure of provider logs, backups, untracked objects, unlinked historic identifiers or processor copies. Those classes remain blocked pending their own reviewed inventory and adapter. Shared fence inventory count/rows describe subject attribution only: unmapped with zero descriptors does not mean zero global rows or settled work. Shared operational classes are always blocked, have no subject selector or erasure adapter, and do not grant runtime table access. Member Realtime topic copies are attributable from retained member sessions after managed session loss; neither provider TTL nor a zero scoped count verifies erasure. Both new classes require blocked policy. Admission archive and working-index classes preserve original history and unknown obligations; logical archival is not deletion or a provider-settlement assertion. History revision counters are shared derived metadata. All four additions remain blocked for personal erasure.
